From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Hi Alyssa —

Fri Mar 6, 12:00–13:00 PST works on our side; I’ve updated the invite (link below). Apologies for the back-and-forth.

I attached an updated set of artifacts and a clearer sequence diagram (v2) addressing your KV cache question. Short answers up front:
- KV cache: Redwood’s runtime can use either an in-node ephemeral cache, a shared Redis cluster, or a managed KV service. For low-latency personalizations we recommend a local LRU cache plus a remote Redis for miss fallback.
- Retention: default session key TTL is configurable per-customer; we support immediate TTL-based eviction and API-based key purge. We’ll include a sample purge API call in the notes.

Attachments included: redwood-arch-pre-read.pdf (v2), sequence_diagram_v2.png, prod-integration-notes.md (updated)

Final agenda — Fri Mar 6, 12:00–13:00 PST (60m):
- 5m: Introductions & objectives
- 20m: Walk the updated sequence diagram (auth flow, request routing, cache behavior)
- 15m: Security & retention controls (KMS/KV, purge APIs, audit logs)
- 15m: Open Q&A and next steps + mutual action plan (owner + dates)

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-falconapps-arch-dive
